newsitem.title: UK: Gilts edge up after US CPI undercuts forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Gilts edge up after US CPI undercuts forecasts.

text.p: UK gilts pushed higher on Wednesday, ignoring higher-than-expected June PSBR data, and lifted by UK earnings data,traders said.
The market was awaiting a batch of U.S. data including June consumer price data. Traders expected the CPI to reinforce the market's upward bias.
U.S. business inventory, industrial production and capacity utilisation will also be scrutinised for signs of any weakness in the health of the U.S. economy.
The September gilt contract was 12/32 higher by 1200 GMT at 114-16, just off the day's highs at 114-17.
June PSBR came in above market expectations at 4.754 billion sterling, but analysts put the figure down to distortions in the timing of VAT receipts and gilt coupon interest payments.

"The market is willing to give the PSBR the benefit of the doubt," one gilts trader said. "We'll have to wait and see if June's lumpy gilt dividends and changes to VAT receipts wash out over the next few months,"
A Reuters poll forecast U.S. June CPI, due to be released at 1230 GMT, to rise by 0.2 percent, compared with an increase of 0.1 percent in May.
Traders said a benign set of UK earnings data helped lift gilts.

"The relatively soft average earnings certainly gave the market a lift," said one gilt trader, who said the minutes from the first Bank of England's monetary policy committee meeting since gaining independence for setting interest rates, helped the long end of the yield curve.
"The monetary policy committee meeting minutes looked pretty hawkish, which caused further flattening of the curve."
But analysts agreed PSBR data would be positive for the gilt market over the next few months.
"The (June) PSBR was always going to show a large deficit," said Darshini David, UK economist at HSBC.
"We were looking for 4.8 billion for June. The PSBR could continue to overshoot in the coming months, but I expect it to meet the government target for the full year."

UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown earlier this month forecast the government's 1997/98 fiscal year PSBR, excluding windfall tax payments from Britain's privatised utilities, would hit 13.25 billion sterling. This compares with a 23.1 billion pound deficit in 1996/97. If the windfall tax returns are included, the full-year PSBR is expected to total 10.9 billion stg.
Short sterling was higher across the board, with September short stg up 0.02 basis points at 92.85, and the December contract up 0.05 at 92.65. -- Simon Gardner, London Newsroom + 44 171 542
